note: Track double-stops (guitar-caged), step 5, on the double-stops-neck tool: 3rds on the G and B strings and 6ths on the G and high e strings at level intermediate (frets 0 to 12), then the 3rds at level advanced (to fret 17), where they come round again an octave up. The text carries no frets: the neck shows them. It states its moves (any key) and mentions no selector.

exercise.title: {{=key}} major in 3rds and 6ths, up the neck
exercise.why: Twelve frets up, a string gives the same note an octave higher, so the 3rds and 6ths from low on the neck carry on in the same order all the way up it.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the 3rds on the G and B strings up to fret 12 and back. Then play them yourself, one double stop per slow beat, and slide your fingers along the strings from each one to the next.
Keep going until each slide stops on the right frets without a second try.

Press Play below to hear the 6ths on the G and high e strings over the same frets. Then play them up and back with the same slides, and keep the B string silent.
Where the shape stays the same, the whole hand slides; where it changes, one finger slides a fret further than the other.

The double stops below now run past fret 12. Play the 3rds from the lowest to the highest and back.
From fret 12 up they are the ones from the bottom of the neck again, an octave higher, and in another key they still come round again twelve frets up.
